title: Pure anticoherent symmetric states
scope: Pure states in Sym^n(C²), indexed by qubit number n and anticoherence order t. Complete core n=2–12; selected exact larger constructions through n=42, including verified Julia formulas and certified fourth-order radical states at n=14, n=17 and n=19.

sources.title: Monogamy relations for symmetric multiqubit systems
sources.authors: Eduardo Serrano-Ensástiga, Olivier Giraud and John Martin
sources.summary: Tables I–III, Appendix A and Theorem 1 supply the symmetric-sector bounds, representative states and the nine-qubit eighth-sector result. Table III includes conjectural optima as well as established results.
sources.notes: Sector/multipole identities and even-only saturation. Full AC must not be inferred from individual even-sector thresholds.

sources.title: Multiqubit monogamy relations beyond shadow inequalities
sources.authors: Eduardo Serrano-Ensástiga, Olivier Giraud, John Martin
sources.summary: Defines Pauli sector lengths and proves bounds for general pure multiqubit states. Bounds attained by symmetric product, GHZ or tetrahedron states also certify extrema within the symmetric subspace.
sources.notes: Global sector constraints usable for separate LP exclusion deductions; not itself a fullAC existence table.

sources.title: Universality in fidelity-based quantum metrology
sources.authors: Luis Aragón-Muñoz, Chryssomalis Chryssomalakos, Ana Gabriela Flores-Delgado, John Martin, Eduardo Serrano-Ensástiga
sources.summary: Expresses orientation-averaged sensing objectives using SU(2)-invariant vectors. Explains why extremal sensing states lie on the boundary of the invariant locus.
sources.notes: Metrological invariant formalism; metrological extrema alone do not certify AC order.

sources.title: Multiqubit symmetric states with high geometric entanglement
sources.authors: J. Martin, O. Giraud, P. A. Braun, D. Braun, T. Bastin
sources.summary: Introduces useful Dicke-basis and Majorana descriptions, and identifies highly geometrically entangled configurations, including tetrahedral and octahedral states.
sources.notes: Geometric entanglement states; objective differs from exact AC.

sources.title: Multiqubit symmetric states with maximally mixed one-qubit reductions
sources.authors: D. Baguette, T. Bastin, J. Martin
sources.summary: Characterizes symmetric states with maximally mixed one-qubit reductions through Dicke coefficients and vanishing collective spin. Provides an explicit four-qubit family containing GHZ and tetrahedron states.
sources.notes: Exact Schmidt-rank bound and Majorana/SLOCC nonexistence criterion.

sources.title: Anticoherence of spin states with point-group symmetries
sources.authors: D. Baguette, F. Damanet, O. Giraud, J. Martin
sources.summary: Relates point-group symmetries of Majorana constellations to anticoherence, supplies low-qubit constructions, and proves existence of anticoherent states of arbitrary order for sufficiently large spins.
sources.notes: Definitions, explicit AC equations, restricted symmetry searches, and constructive all-order existence.

sources.title: Anticoherence measures for pure spin states
sources.summary: Defines purity-based anticoherence A_t=(t+1)(1−Tr rho_t^2)/t, gives explicit cat and tetrahedron states, and studies the existence of states with degenerate Majorana constellations.
sources.notes: Small-spin numerical survey, explicit warning that missing solutions are numerical; exact low-order families.

sources.title: Entanglement robustness against particle loss in multiqubit systems
sources.authors: A. Neven, J. Martin, T. Bastin
sources.summary: Characterizes pure entangled states that lose all entanglement after losing one qubit and relates symmetric-state robustness to SLOCC classes.
sources.notes: Particle-loss entanglement and reduction ranks; no further exact AC-order exclusion extracted.

sources.title: Tensor Representation of Spin States
sources.authors: O. Giraud, D. Braun, D. Baguette, T. Bastin, J. Martin
sources.summary: Builds spin operators by projecting Pauli strings onto the symmetric subspace and characterizes anticoherence through maximally mixed reduced states and vanishing multipoles.
sources.notes: Tensor/reduced-state formalism; no additional unconditional small-size exclusion extracted.

sources.title: Extreme depolarization for any spin
sources.summary: Provides a spin-to-symmetric-qubit dictionary and explicit highly anticoherent states, and relates isotropic and anisotropic depolarization to entanglement and multipole structure.
sources.notes: The multipole characterization is used here. Two Table IV rows on p.17 require the corrections documented above: the nine-qubit order is 2, and the ten-qubit printed coefficients are misnormalized.

sources.title: Optimal Detection of Rotations about Unknown Axes by Coherent and Anticoherent States
sources.authors: John Martin, Stefan Weigert, Olivier Giraud
sources.summary: Writes average rotation fidelity in terms of anticoherence measures and gives explicit low-spin candidate states, including the tetrahedron, triangular bipyramid and octahedron.
sources.notes: Explicit small-spin nonexistence statements, not accompanied by the needed global exclusion proofs here.

sources.title: ACLiege: explicit states and anticoherent subspaces
sources.authors: John Martin; credits in the source include M. Grassl
sources.notes: Supplied Julia source, read without executing it. Sixteen pure-state formulas and ten subspace bases were independently checked exactly. Decimal-only and malformed records are distinguished in the audit.

proofs.title: Schmidt-rank obstruction
proofs.summary: The anticoherent reduction must have full rank in its symmetric subspace; the complementary subsystem must be large enough to accommodate the same Schmidt spectrum.
proofs.bodyHtml: The two complementary reductions have the same nonzero Schmidt spectrum. Anticoherence requires \rho_t=I_{t+1}/(t+1), of rank t+1. The complement is supported on \operatorname{Sym}^{n-t}(\mathbb C^2), of dimension n-t+1. Hence t+1\le n-t+1.

proofs.title: Odd-size complement obstruction
proofs.summary: A one-dimensional complementary kernel would itself have an impossible Schmidt rank.
proofs.bodyHtml:
If \rho_t=I_{t+1}/(t+1), its complement \rho_{t+1} has t+1 equal nonzero eigenvalues in a symmetric space of dimension t+2. Thus \rho_{t+1}=(I_{t+2}-|\phi\rangle\langle\phi|)/(t+1) for a normalized symmetric (t+1)-qubit vector |\phi\rangle.

Trace one qubit, using \operatorname{Tr}_1 I_{\mathrm{sym}}^{(t+1)}=\frac{t+2}{t+1}I_{\mathrm{sym}}^{(t)}. Comparing with \rho_t yields \rho_t^\phi=I_{t+1}/(t+1). But \rho_t^\phi has rank at most two because |\phi\rangle has a single-qubit complement. This contradicts t+1\ge3.

references.location: Schmidt-rank framework; the odd-complement deduction is newly supplied by the catalogue

proofs.title: Spin-tensor Gram obstruction
proofs.summary: The spin-tensor Gram matrix gives a quadratic necessary condition on the number of qubits.
proofs.bodyHtml:
Put q=\lfloor t/2\rfloor. For Hilbert–Schmidt orthonormal tensors A,B of ranks at most q, the product A^\dagger B has ranks at most 2q\le t. Anticoherence therefore gives \langle\psi|A^\dagger B|\psi\rangle=\operatorname{Tr}(A^\dagger B)/(n+1).

The (q+1)^2 vectors A|\psi\rangle consequently have a positive diagonal Gram matrix, so they are linearly independent in the (n+1)-dimensional spin space.

proofs.title: Eight qubits cannot be fourth-order AC
proofs.summary: An exact two-copy identity would give a negative total-spin probability if all multipoles through rank four vanished.
proofs.bodyHtml: Here p_J is the total-spin-J probability of two copies, and a_L is the nonnegative squared length of rank-L spin multipoles. Fourth-order anticoherence sets a_1,\ldots,a_4 to zero, forcing p_0=-4/27, a contradiction. The coefficient identity is checked with exact rational arithmetic.

references.location: Multipole/purity convention; this exclusion identity is an independent catalogue calculation

proofs.title: Nine qubits cannot be third-order AC
proofs.summary: An exact four-copy positivity certificate proves the previously reported exclusion for every pure symmetric nine-qubit state.

references.location: Sec. 4.4.3 reports absence; the exact proof is independently derived in this catalogue.

proofs.bodyHtml:
Average four copies of a hypothetical third-order anticoherent state over collective rotations. The resulting operator X is positive, has \operatorname{Tr}X=1, and obeys exact linear contraction equations from its vanishing rank-one, rank-two and rank-three multipoles.

In an explicit angular-momentum basis, eighty-five independent rational equations leave a three-dimensional space of candidates. Four diagonal coordinates obey a strictly positive linear relation summing to zero. Positivity forces all four coordinates to vanish; they determine the remaining three parameters, hence X=0. This contradicts \operatorname{Tr}X=1.

The derivation handles arbitrary complex amplitudes. Independent exact verifiers reconstruct the equations and check the positive relation and rank calculations.

Read the complete four-copy proof ↗ · Exact certificate · Independent verifier

proofs.title: Ten qubits cannot be fourth-order AC
proofs.summary: An exact degree-six polynomial identity proves the previously reported exclusion for every pure symmetric ten-qubit state.

references.location: Sec. 4.4.4 reports absence; the exact proof is independently derived in this catalogue.

proofs.bodyHtml:
For every pure spin-five vector, an exact identity expresses \lVert\psi\rVert^6 as a rational linear combination of twenty cubic scalar contractions of its spin multipoles. Every term contains a multipole of rank 1\le L\le4. Fourth-order anticoherence would make the entire right-hand side zero, contradicting \lVert\psi\rVert^6=1.

Two independent exact calculations establish the identity: one on the symmetric three-copy space, and one by expanding all polynomial coefficients in arbitrary complex amplitudes. No symmetry ansatz or numerical tolerance is used in the final certificate.

Read the complete identity and proof ↗ · Exact certificate · Independent verifier

proofs.title: Ten qubits cannot be fifth-order AC
proofs.summary: A second exact two-copy identity rules out fifth-order anticoherence.
proofs.bodyHtml: Fifth-order anticoherence sets a_1,\ldots,a_5 to zero, forcing p_6=-27/187. A probability cannot be negative. The coefficient identity is checked with exact rational arithmetic.

references.location: Multipole/purity convention; this exclusion identity is an independent catalogue calculation

proofs.title: Eleven qubits cannot be fourth-order AC
proofs.summary: Two exact three-copy certificates exclude fourth-order anticoherence for arbitrary complex pure symmetric eleven-qubit states.

references.location: Earlier numerical survey; the exact exclusion is independently derived in this catalogue.

proofs.bodyHtml:
A pure fourth-order anticoherent eleven-qubit state would produce a positive, rotation-invariant three-copy operator X with \operatorname{Tr}X=1. Its low-rank multipoles impose twenty-seven necessary equations on twenty-seven real block coordinates. Their integer matrix A satisfies \det A\equiv3\pmod{37}, so it is invertible. The equations force X=0, a contradiction. Taking real parts of positive blocks handles arbitrary complex states.

A second exact certificate expresses \lVert\psi\rVert^6 as a sum of twenty-six cubic multipole invariants. Every term contains a rank between one and four, so fourth-order anticoherence would force 1=0. Its full polynomial expansion is verified coefficientwise with rational arithmetic.

This proves that the maximal order at n=11 is three. Combined with the smaller-size exclusions and a twelve-qubit witness, it also proves that twelve is the first qubit number admitting a pure fourth-order anticoherent state.

Read both proofs and their exact certificates ↗ · LaTeX proof · Polynomial verifier

proofs.title: Thirteen qubits cannot be fourth-order AC
proofs.summary: An exact four-copy invariant-moment certificate forces the trace of a hypothetical normalized state moment to vanish.
proofs.bodyHtml:
Average four copies of a hypothetical fourth-order AC state over collective rotations. The resulting invariant operator X is positive and has \operatorname{Tr}X=1. Vanishing multipoles of ranks one through four impose exact linear contraction equations.

There are 320 independent constraints on 331 real multiplicity coordinates. Their eleven-dimensional kernel is annihilated by the physical trace functional, as established with exact rational arithmetic. The constraints therefore force \operatorname{Tr}X=0, a contradiction. The proof covers arbitrary complex states; no restricted support, symmetry ansatz or numerical infeasibility claim is used.

Every higher AC order is excluded by nesting. The existing exact third-order thirteen-qubit representative consequently has globally maximum AC order three.

references.title: Complete four-copy proof and exact certificates

proofs.title: Rectangular spin-tensor obstruction at every order
proofs.summary: Orthogonal rectangular spin-tensor images strengthen the necessary qubit count, excluding (N,t)=(15,6),(16,7),(17,7),(18,7).
proofs.bodyHtml:
For a pure t-AC state, choose Hilbert–Schmidt orthonormal tensor maps from spin n/2 to spin (n-h)/2, with ranks at most t/2. Every pairwise product has rank at most t, so the tensor images have a positive diagonal Gram matrix. Counting the available output dimensions for all shifts h gives the displayed conditions.

At sixth order the minimum permitted size is sixteen; at seventh order it is twenty. These necessary conditions apply to arbitrary complex states. They do not establish existence at equality.

references.title: General bound and proof in the AC-subspace catalogue

proofs.title: Sixteen qubits cannot be sixth-order AC
proofs.summary: At equality the rectangular tensor channel forces an additional vanishing multipole and contradicts the seventh-order dimension count.
proofs.bodyHtml:
Fifteen rank-one, rank-two and rank-three tensor images of a hypothetical sixth-order AC state would fill the spin-seven output space, so their covariant channel sends its projector to I_{15}/17. The rank-seven channel multiplier is exactly 5\sqrt{69}/8398\ne0; rank seven must therefore vanish too.

The state would be seventh-order AC, requiring twenty orthogonal tensor images in dimension sixteen. This is impossible. Higher orders are excluded by nesting. Exact physical tensors and an independent Clebsch–Gordan calculation verify the multiplier.

references.title: Full proof and exact channel checks

proofs.title: Twenty qubits cannot be seventh-order AC
proofs.summary: Saturation of the seventh-order tensor count would force eighth-order AC, whose minimum qubit count is twenty-five.
proofs.bodyHtml:
The twenty rectangular tensor images of a hypothetical seventh-order AC state would fill their twenty-dimensional output space. The associated covariant channel must have scalar output. Its rank-eight multiplier is nonzero, so the input rank-eight multipoles vanish as well.

Eighth-order AC requires n\ge25, contradicting n=20. This is an exact equality obstruction, not a numerical search failure.

references.title: General equality obstruction and exact multipliers

proofs.title: Fourteen qubits cannot be fifth-order AC
proofs.summary: An exact three-copy positivity certificate excludes fifth-order anticoherence for arbitrary complex pure fourteen-qubit states.
proofs.bodyHtml:
Average three copies of a hypothetical fifth-order AC state over collective rotations. The positive invariant moment has trace one and is supported on the 680-dimensional space \operatorname{Sym}^3(V_7).

Its low-rank contraction equations have exact rank 45 on 47 real invariant coordinates. On the entire kernel, the exact physical identity is 265256992\operatorname{Tr}X+26961161975p_4+118909381500p_{16}=0, where p_J is the total-spin probability of the three-copy moment. Unit trace and nonnegative probabilities contradict this equality.

The supplied exact verifier reconstructs the equations and checks the ranks, kernel and positive relation. The proof applies to arbitrary complex amplitudes. Together with the fourth-order radical witness it proves that the maximum pure-state AC order is four.

proofs.title: Fifteen qubits cannot be fourth-order AC
proofs.summary: An exact four-copy certificate uses positivity of the moment and its partial transpose to exclude every pure fourth-order AC state.
proofs.bodyHtml:
A fourth-order AC state would give a positive trace-one rotationally averaged four-copy moment X on \operatorname{Sym}^4(V_{15/2}). Its vanishing low multipoles give 525 necessary contraction equations on 579 real invariant coordinates.

This moment is a mixture of product projectors across the first copy and the remaining three, so its partial transpose is positive too. After spin flip, its positive invariant blocks are Y_L. An exact rational combination of the equations gives 0=\operatorname{Tr}X+\sum_J\operatorname{Tr}(C_JB_J)+\sum_L\operatorname{Tr}(Q_LY_L), where B_J denotes the certificate’s dyadically rescaled input coefficient matrices, Y_L its positive output matrix compressions, and all dual blocks are strictly positive definite. The right side is at least one, a contradiction.

All 150 input and 522 output positivity pivots are checked with exact rational arithmetic. An independent verifier reconstructs the physical equations and partial-transpose map. This covers arbitrary complex states. The existing exact third-order state therefore has globally maximum AC order three.

proofs.title: Seventeen qubits cannot be fifth-order AC
proofs.summary: An exact three-copy partial-transpose positivity certificate excludes every pure fifth-order AC state.
proofs.bodyHtml:
A hypothetical fifth-order AC state would give a positive trace-one rotationally averaged three-copy moment X on \operatorname{Sym}^3(V_{17/2}). Its vanishing low multipoles give 62 necessary contraction equations on 72 real invariant coordinates. As a mixture of product projectors, its partial transpose is positive too.

After spin flip, let Y_L denote its positive output compressions and x_J the certificate’s dyadically rescaled input coefficient matrices. An exact rational combination gives 0=\operatorname{Tr}X+\sum_J\operatorname{Tr}(C_Jx_J)+\sum_L\operatorname{Tr}(Q_LY_L), with all dual matrices strictly positive definite. The right side is at least one, a contradiction.

Independent reconstruction verifies every physical equation and all 171 positive rational LDL pivots. The proof covers arbitrary complex amplitudes. The existing exact fourth-order radical state therefore has globally maximum AC order four.

references.title: Full proof and exact rational certificate

proofs.title: A rank-one complement excludes sixth order at seventeen qubits
proofs.summary: A hypothetical state would produce a pure sixth-order AC complement on fifteen qubits, contradicting the rectangular tensor count.
proofs.bodyHtml:
The fifteen Hilbert–Schmidt orthonormal rectangular tensors of ranks one through three from spin 17/2 to 15/2 give orthogonal images with Gram matrix I_{15}/18. Their scaled projector has a one-dimensional complement in dimension sixteen.

The complete tensor multiplets make this channel covariant, so the complementary pure state inherits the vanishing multipoles through rank six. It would be a pure sixth-order AC state on fifteen qubits. The same tensor count would then require fifteen orthogonal vectors in fourteen dimensions, which is impossible.

The general argument excludes N=(r+1)^2+1 at order 2r for every integer r\ge1. This short analytical proof is independent of the stronger fifth-order exclusion.

proofs.title: Eighteen qubits cannot be sixth-order AC
proofs.summary: An exact positive three-copy trace–probability identity excludes every pure sixth-order AC state.
proofs.bodyHtml:
A hypothetical sixth-order AC state would give a positive trace-one rotationally averaged moment X on \operatorname{Sym}^3(V_9), of dimension 1330. Eighty independent exact equations on 84 invariant coordinates leave a four-dimensional kernel.

Throughout that kernel, \alpha\operatorname{Tr}X+\beta_1p_1+\beta_3p_3+\beta_4p_4+\beta_6p_6=0, where p_J is the physical total-spin probability and all five coefficients are explicit strictly positive integers. Trace one and nonnegative probabilities contradict this identity.

An independent exact verifier reconstructs every equation, the full kernel and all 25 probabilities from every magnetic descendant. The proof covers arbitrary complex states. The existing Julia-source fifth-order state therefore has globally maximum AC order five.

references.title: Full identity, proof and integer certificate
Fifth-order witness and optimal subspace dimension

proofs.title: Nineteen qubits cannot be sixth-order AC
proofs.summary: An exact positive three-copy trace–probability identity excludes every pure sixth-order AC state.
proofs.bodyHtml:
A hypothetical sixth-order AC state gives a positive trace-one rotationally averaged three-copy moment X on \operatorname{Sym}^3(V_{19/2}), of dimension 1540. Eighty-eight independent exact contraction equations on 94 real invariant coordinates leave a six-dimensional kernel.

On this entire kernel, \alpha\operatorname{Tr}X+\sum_J\beta_Jp_J=0, where J\in\{3/2,5/2,15/2,17/2,19/2,39/2\}, and every coefficient is an explicit strictly positive integer. Trace one and nonnegative probabilities contradict this identity.

The independent verifier reconstructs the complete representation, selected equations, full kernel and every physical probability using exact arithmetic. This excludes arbitrary complex states and all higher orders.

proofs.title: Nineteen qubits cannot be fifth-order AC
proofs.summary: An exact four-copy matrix-positivity certificate excludes every pure fifth-order AC state.
proofs.bodyHtml:
A hypothetical fifth-order AC state gives a positive trace-one rotationally averaged moment X on \operatorname{Sym}^4(V_{19/2}), of dimension 8855. Its 37 spin sectors supply 1522 real symmetric multiplicity coordinates. The vanishing low multipoles imply 1380 selected physical contraction equations.

An exact rational combination gives 0=\operatorname{Tr}X+\sum_J\operatorname{Tr}(C_Jx_J), where x_J\succeq0 are the certificate’s rescaled moment matrices and every C_J\succ0. The right side is at least one, which is impossible. The independent verifier reconstructs every equation and all physical trace factors, and checks 277 strictly positive rational factorization pivots.

The proof covers arbitrary complex amplitudes. Together with the five-component radical fourth-order state, it proves that the maximum pure AC order at nineteen qubits is four. Every higher order is excluded by nesting.

proofs.title: Twenty qubits cannot be sixth-order AC
proofs.summary: An exact three-copy matrix-positivity certificate excludes every pure sixth-order AC state.
proofs.bodyHtml:
A hypothetical sixth-order state supplies a positive trace-one invariant three-copy moment on , of dimension 1771. Its 29 spin sectors give 108 real symmetric multiplicity coordinates. Vanishing multipoles impose 95 selected physical contraction equations.

An exact rational combination gives , where are the rescaled physical moment matrices and every . The right side is at least one, a contradiction. The independent verifier reconstructs the full representation, every selected equation and trace, and all 61 positive rational factorization pivots.

This covers arbitrary complex states. The existing exact fifth-order Julia-source witness therefore has globally maximum pure AC order five; all higher orders are excluded by nesting.

sourceCaveats: Order means at least t. Every t-AC state is also s-AC for s ≤ t; a witness does not prove that t is the largest possible order at that qubit number.
Full anticoherence requires every multipole rank 1,…,t to vanish. Cancelling only even multipoles, or attaining an even-sector lower bound, does not suffice.
The symmetric t-body identity has dimension t+1, not 2^t. These states are distinct from absolutely maximally entangled qubit states.
PRResearch 4, 013178 (2022), PDF p.17 Table IV labels a nine-qubit state order 3 although its rank-three multipole and reduced matrix are nonzero. Its verified order is 2.

The same 2022 table prints ten-qubit coefficients with squared norm 43/55. Replacing the two endpoint amplitudes 1/√11 by 1/√5 gives a normalized third-order state; this is an independently checked correction, not a published erratum.
Blank cells in the 2017 numerical survey mean failed convergence. Restricted cyclic-construction thresholds in the 2015 paper are not universal existence thresholds.

The eleven-qubit third-order representative with radical complex amplitudes is independently derived and exactly checked here; it is not attributed to the rounded numerical vector in the 2017 appendix.
definition: A pure symmetric N-qubit state is t-anticoherent iff rho_t is the maximally mixed state I_(t+1)/(t+1) on the symmetric t-qubit subspace. Equivalently all spin moments through order t are independent of direction. This requires every multipole rank1,...,t to vanish, not only the even ranks.

constructions.title: Order one at every size
constructions.text: For every n ≥ 2, the GHZ / spin-cat state is first-order anticoherent.

constructions.title: Order three for every even n ≥ 8
constructions.text: The support gaps remove all off-diagonal moments through rank three; symmetric weights give the required diagonal moments.

constructions.title: Every fixed order eventually occurs
constructions.text: The constructive quadrature argument proves existence for sufficiently large n at every fixed t. Its restricted search thresholds are not minimal universal thresholds.

references.location: Sec. VI; proof continues on PDF p.11

validation.method: Exact symbolic normalization and every reduced matrix through the achieved order. Two-copy identities, three-copy polynomial and moment certificates, and a four-copy positivity certificate use exact arithmetic with independent verification. Cross-catalogue rectangular-tensor theorems and the sixteen-qubit equality obstruction are included; both imported radical witnesses are rechecked independently.
